notes: Merged implementation skill (absorbs implement-feature, fix-bug, and the Mode A / test-authoring half of unit-test and integration-test). Holds Write/Edit, produces NO verdicts -- review, security scan, and test execution (Mode B) move to cbr-verify, a separate no-Write skill. Evaluate that: the TECH-spec precondition stop fires correctly; code + UTC.md + ITC.md all get produced; ITC test cases are business-flow chains tracing BASIC section 6.5 through TECH section 4.3, not CRUD-unit dressed up as integration tests; the fix-loop's 2-round escalation to systematic debugging fires; and -- the most safety-critical assertion -- cbr-implement never spawns cbr-reviewer or cbr-tester as a grading/verdict role, and never produces a verdict artifact itself, regardless of mode.

evals.prompt: Implement the order module controllers and services from the TECH spec at docs/streams/order-20260804/design/TECH.md.
evals.expected_output: Step 0 confirms TECH.md exists. Step 1 implements following the detected framework's module order (ORM/DTOs/services/controllers or equivalent), applying soft delete filter, audit columns, auth+role guards, input validation, API docs -- citing references/coding-patterns.md for the pattern detail. Step 2 authors docs/streams/order-20260804/test-cases/UTC.md and ITC.md alongside (never executes them). Step 3 checks the live diff against simplify thresholds. Step 4 runs self-check, writes docs/streams/order-20260804/work-logs/DEV-[YYYYMMDD].md, then stops naming cbr-verify as next -- does NOT spawn any reviewer/tester itself.

evals.prompt: Implement the checkout feature, but there's no TECH spec for it yet.
evals.expected_output: precondition-stop. Step 0 finds no docs/streams/checkout-*/design/TECH.md, STOPS immediately: 'Cannot implement -- the TECH spec doesn't exist yet... run cbr-plan to produce it.' Does not approximate or infer the missing spec, does not write any code.

evals.prompt: Write unit tests for the PaymentService and integration tests for the checkout workflow.
evals.expected_output: Step 2 (Unit-ModeA + Integration-ModeA) runs. UTC.md covers auth/RBAC, CRUD happy paths, business-workflow transitions, input validation, soft delete. ITC.md is a BUSINESS-FLOW CHAIN -- at least 3 business steps spanning at least 2 actors/modules, tracing BASIC.md section 6.5's BF-xxx rows through TECH.md section 4.3's implementation mapping, NOT a sequence of isolated CRUD calls on one actor. Both documents only -- neither is executed. Workers spawned (if --parallel) are cbr-developer, never cbr-tester.

evals.prompt: Fix the failing login test -- it's throwing a 401 even with a valid token.
evals.expected_output: Fix-loop direct-fix path: reads the failing report/reproduction, roots the cause by layer (auth middleware, token handling), applies a minimal-blast-radius fix (no surrounding refactor), verifies with the affected test then full regression, writes docs/streams/[feature]-*/bug-reports/BUG-[YYYYMMDD]-[nn].md with root cause + fix + verification.

evals.prompt: The webhook signature bug fix has now failed 2 rounds in a row -- same intermittent failure keeps recurring.
evals.expected_output: escalation. After the 2nd failed round, STOPS patching symptoms and loads references/systematic-debugging.md, working its 4-phase methodology (reproduce, isolate, root cause, fix and verify) instead of attempting a 3rd direct-fix guess. Notes this 2-round threshold is distinct from the project's 3-strike rule -- it counts attempts at this one bug, not consecutive different approaches.

evals.prompt: Implementation is done and the work log is written -- go ahead and review the code for quality and security issues, then run the test suite as the gate.
evals.expected_output: Should route to cbr-verify / not fire for the review+security+test-execution part. cbr-implement's own Step 4 already stopped and named cbr-verify as next; this skill holds no Write-adjacent review/scan/test-execution responsibility and produces no verdict artifact under any mode, including --auto (which invokes cbr-verify via the Skill tool rather than doing the work itself).

evals.prompt: Design the ORM schema and API endpoints for the notifications feature.
evals.expected_output: Should route to cbr-plan / not fire, because this asks for technical design (TECH spec authoring), which is cbr-plan's Tech-Design phase, not implementation of an already-designed spec.

evals.prompt: cbr-implement checkout -- resume implementing this feature in a brand-new session; its plan/PLAN.md was written earlier and has several unchecked phases.
evals.expected_output: cross-session task pickup. At Step 1 entry, TaskList returns empty (tasks died with the old session), so cbr-implement re-hydrates from plan/PLAN.md's unchecked [ ] phase items (already-[x] items are done, skipped) rather than re-doing completed work -- per references/task-management.md. If the Task tools error entirely, it falls back to working straight from PLAN.md's unchecked items. Then implements normally.

evals.prompt: I finished implementing phases 2 and 3 of the checkout feature -- the work log is written and self-check passes.
evals.expected_output: sync-back at Step 4 / Hand-off. Before stopping, cbr-implement TaskUpdates the session tasks to their real status and backfills plan/PLAN.md -- flipping [ ] -> [x] for every completed phase across ALL phases (not just this batch), updating PLAN.md's status line and STREAM.md's board from the actual checkbox state. A completed task that maps to no phase is reported, not silently marked done. Then names cbr-verify as next and stops -- no verdict produced here.

evals.prompt: cbr-implement order-management --team 3 -- this feature has independent backend, frontend, and webhook modules.
evals.expected_output: team mode. First checks CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 is set (if not, STOPS and tells the user -- never silently degrades to --parallel) and confirms the token cost with the user. Writes a file-ownership map (backend/frontend/webhook disjoint, shared files like routers/migrations kept for the lead), then spawns 3 NAMED cbr-developer teammates in one message (naming is what enrols them as real team members with SendMessage/Task tools -- an unnamed spawn would be a plain worker), each with its owned paths and the hard File-Ownership Rules (optionally isolation:'worktree', provisioning hooks in the worktree first per team-mode.md, or file-ownership alone). Teammates coordinate live (claim tasks, escalate conflicts to the lead); lead integrates the shared files + runs Self-Check across the merged result + writes ONE work log, then shutdown_requests each teammate. Per references/team-mode.md -- no TeamCreate needed.

evals.prompt: cbr-implement checkout --team 3, but CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS is not set in this environment.
evals.expected_output: team-precondition negative. Because CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 is absent, --team STOPS with a clear message telling the user to enable agent teams (e.g. via claudebrew install) -- it does NOT silently fall back to --parallel's unnamed fire-and-collect workers, since that would quietly deliver a weaker execution model than the user asked for.
